own_solution.law: Successive resonances satisfy L + e = (2n + 1)c/(4f), so their separation is ΔL = c/(2f). Thus Δt = c/(2fv) = 343/(2 × 512 × 0.015).
assumptions: The stated resonance model and fixed end correction apply throughout.
The water surface falls uniformly between the two resonances.
The tube permits two successive resonances.

uncertain_fields: T9749: whether the increased withdrawal rate applies only before the first resonance or persists afterward.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T3D7A and TB8E5 replace the explicit 0.9 cm/s increment in their corresponding variants TF4FF and T49F8 with an unspecified 'small amount', violating the requirement that variants preserve the number and unit.

counterexamples.description: If the increase established before the first resonance persists, the speed between resonances is 2.4 cm/s and the interval is 13.9567057292 s; if the increase applies only before the first resonance, the interval remains 22.3307291667 s.

notes: The base problem is well posed under its explicitly supplied acoustic model. T9749 is assigned D under the reading that the changed rate applies only before the first resonance; its wording also permits a persistent increase. TEA1B is interpreted as an explicit update of the baseline speed to 2.4 cm/s. Initial air length contributes an offset to resonance times that cancels in their difference. Radius can influence the fixed end correction, which also cancels under the stated model. The pond has no stated connection to the tube. The two 130 cm sentences match each other, as do the two 2.6 cm sentences. No outside information was accessed.
